title: The 1963 studio session with Don Redman arrangements
summary: Moore's group recorded tracks arranged by Don Redman that were not released until he put them out himself.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Well, listen, on some of your two recordings -- one of your recordings you have some tracks that were made in 1963 which you have "Black and Blue," Chant of the Weed" and "Panama" as well as "Blues My Naughty Sweetie Gives to Me," "Chatez La Bas," and "I Ain't Got Nobody." This is Mundell Lowe playing guitar and George Duvivier or Milt Hinton playing bass and either Bobby Donaldson or Cliff Leeman on drums and a very fine pinao player by the name of Hank Jones. Was that a studio recording or was that a band that you kind of --
No, that was a studio recording.
A studio recording. It was a band that you led for the studio?
Yes, and Don Redman wrote the arrangements.
And it never came out until just recently, these particular tracks?
You mentioned about the numbers that I have on my album?
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
Well, as I say, Don Redman wrote the arrangements, but I think that the pieces that you mentioned, "Chant of the Weed" and what were the others?
"Black and Blue," "Panama," "Chatez La Bas," I Ain't Got Nobody," Blues My Naughty Sweetie Gives Me."
One of the large record companies recorded that but never released it and a number of years have passed by so I just put them out myself. So that's how those numbers on that album.....
